textbookText: Figure: 9.2.9 some migratory fishes Factors influencing fish migration i. Physical factors: Physical factors are light intensity, temperature, water current, turbidity and depth of water etc. These factors influence fish migration. Any change or alterations in any of these physical factors compel fish to migrate for searching their favourable environment. For example those fishes which tend to remain in clear or less turbid water migrate for searching such places as the water of stream, river etc. become more turbid in rainy season. ii. Chemical factors: These factors consist of salinity of water, smell, pH, taste of water, dissolved oxygen and overall water chemistry that influence in fish migration. iii. Biological factors: They are gonadial activity of fish, hormones (FSH) secreted by endocrine glands, availability of food, predators etc.

Types of fish migration Various types of fish migration can be discussed as follow: 1. Diadromous migration: Truly migratory fishes like Salmon, Hilsa, Anguilla, Gobbies etc. perform this type of migration. In this, Migration occurs from sea water to fresh water and vice versa. It is further divided into following types: i. Anadromous migration: Some marine fishes migrate toward freshwater mainly for breeding or reproduction which is called anadromous migration. Example: Salmon, Sea lamprey, Hilsa, Shad etc. Various changes that occur in the body of fish during migration are accumulation of reserve food, maturation of gonad, degeneration of alimentary canal etc. After the breeding process is over, young ones and adult return to their original home ground or feeding places. ii. Catadromous migration: Some freshwater fishes which migrate to sea water or marine water for reproduction which is called catadromous migration. Example: Eel (Anguilla bengalensis) which is found in river system of Nepal migrate to Bay of Bengal. Various changes that occur in the body of fish during migration are Biology, Grade 11 | 451

suspended feeding, maturation of gonad, degeneration of alimentary canal, body colour become silver white from yellow etc. iii. Amphidromous migration: The type migration which occurs from ocean water to fresh water and freshwater to ocean water for feeding purpose instead of reproduction. Example: gobies fishes. 2. Potadromous migration: When fish migration is confined only within freshwater, it is called potadromous migration. Example: carp fishes, trout etc. 3. Oceanodromous migration: The migration of fishes which is confined only to marine water or sea water is called oceanodromus migration. 4. Alimental migration: Migration of fishes for feeding purpose is called alimental migration. Example: sharks, carps etc. 5. Shoreward migration: migration of fishes towards sea shore or bank of river is called shoreward migration. Example: Anabas 6. Vertical migration: Migration of fishes from bottom or depth of water to the surface and in the reverse direction is called vertical migration. Example: sword fish, meckerel etc. 7. Latitudinal migration: Migration of fish from north to south and vice versa. Example: sword fish, hammer headed shark etc. 8. Climatic migration: fishes migrate in response to change in season or climate for seeking safe place is called climatic migration.

Advantages of fish migration 1. Migration ensures abundant supply of food, suitable breeding ground and shelter. 2. It also provides suitable condition for the survival of juveniles in the migrated place from enemies. 3. Migration also protects fishes from adverse environmental situations. 4. Some ichthyologists believe that migration is an adaptation towards abundance.

2. MIGRATION IN BIRDS Migration of various types of birds is a fascinating and spectacular event associated with bird life. Many birds can be seen flying in the sky from one place to another. According to Cahn (1935), “Migration is the periodic passing of animals from one place to another”. Migration in birds can also be defined as the regular and periodic passing of birds from their breeding and nesting ground to feeding and resting ground. Such movement occurs during the particular period of the year and the birds usually follow the same route. Some migratory birds are Siberian crane, golden plover of USA, black and white cuckoos, robins, hawk, crane, geese etc.Those birds which do not migrate and remain in their home ground all the time are called resident birds. Example: Bob white, ruffled sand grouse etc.
